summary: Early 429s during mass concurrent upload/transform job causing client failures
description:
Issue summary:
Atlas Analytics reports that large nightly data-transformation jobs (multipart uploads + per-record embedding calls) started receiving 429 responses from our API at the beginning of their run window. The 429s are returned within ~200-400ms of POSTing, before most backend processing begins — customer calls these 'early 429s'.

Impact:
- Customer batch job (approx 30k small records, ~700 concurrent connections from a single API key) fails to complete; observed ~18% of requests return 429s within first 5 minutes.
- Affects downstream ETL; client retries amplify spike and lead to backoff cascades.

Environment:
- Production, us-east region, dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for Atlas Analytics.
- Customer using SDK v1.4.2 with default concurrency settings.
- Affected model: redwood-open-7b-v2.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Initiate 700 parallel POST /v1/embeddings requests with 100 items per request.
2) Keep connections open; SDK defaults to no additional client-side jitter/backoff on initial failures.
3) Observe 429s returned within 200-400ms of request start.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 2
- Support console shows per-API-key token consumption jumps to bucket exhaustion within 30s of the run start.
- Serving runtime traces show low per-request processing time; queuing at the API gateway and quota-enforcer is the choke point.

Expected behavior:
- Gateway should allow reasonable short bursts for dedicated/enterprise keys given reserved capacity, or return 202/queued indicator rather than immediate 429s for in-flight requests that could be satisfied by the dedicated pool.

Relevant logs (snippets):
- [2026-03-10T02:01:12Z] api-gateway: request id=abc123 key=atlas-prod status=429 reason=rate_limit_remaining=0 ttl_ms=210
- [2026-03-10T02:01:12Z] quota-enforcer: key=atlas-prod tokens_before=0 tokens_after=-1 burst_allowed=false
- [2026-03-10T02:01:12Z] serving-runtime: accept_latency_ms=8 process_ms=12 model:redwood-open-7b-v2

Notes: Customer asserts this pattern only began after they increased parallel workers to handle a growth in dataset size. They did not change SDK version.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start 700 concurrent connections using Atlas API key to POST embeddings in parallel. 2) Observe initial 429s within 200-400ms. 3) Note X-RateLimit-Remaining header = 0 and Retry-After present.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Khan (Support): Logged initial report from Atlas. Collected request IDs and top-line console metrics. Escalated to Dedicated Pool team.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Atlas Analytics (customer): Provided reproduction script and timestamps. Reports runs always start at 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-10 12:30 - Diego Marquez (SRE): Confirmed 429s in logs for keys; I see token bucket hitting 0 quickly. Sharing dashboards: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/atlas/throttling-overview
2026-03-10 13:45 - Priya Menon (Product): Asked if burst reservoir for dedicated pools is enabled — confirming config for atlas-prod shows burst_reservoir=0 (unexpected for enterprise).
2026-03-11 09:22 - Diego Marquez (SRE): Temporarily increased per-key burst allowance to 2500 tokens for atlas-prod; monitor for 2 hours. Customer asked us to keep change if stable.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Atlas Analytics: After temporary increase, early 429s dropped to <0.5% of requests. They will stagger job start next run as additional safety measure.
investigation_notes: Throttle behavior: quota-enforcer uses token-bucket keyed by api_key + route. Default burst reservoir for dedicated keys unexpectedly set to 0 due to migration bug in 2025-11 (see INT-532).

Traffic pattern: very steep slope at run start (700 concurrent new TCP connections) – token bucket refill cannot amortize that instantaneous demand, leading to early 429s even though serving runtime has capacity.
Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit values reflect configured steady-state capacity not burst reservoir; customers assume short bursts will be supported for dedicated tiers.

Hypothesis: two contributing issues – (1) burst_reservoir config lost for some enterprise dedicated tenants during earlier config migration; (2) api-gateway enforces token check pre-routing, so requests are rejected before the scheduler can route to idle GPUs that could handle the spike.
Dashboards checked: per-key qps, per-route queue length, dedicated-pool idle GPU count (showing 4 idle GPUs at spike time), quota-enforcer reject rate.
Related PR: runtime change to move token check later in request path (so short bursts can be served) is under discussion at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891.
Customer-side mitigation: stagger start or use client-side limited concurrency and exponential backoff with jitter — immediate recommendation shared.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation applied on 2026-03-11: increased per-key burst_reservoir to 2500 for atlas-prod and enabled soft-queueing for short window (30s) on gateway. Result: early 429s dropped from ~18% to <0.5% for two monitored runs.

Permanent fix plan: engineering to revert the migration bug that set burst_reservoir=0 for some dedicated tenants (patch PR referenced). We will also add a configuration audit to detect zero-reservoir values for enterprise/dedicated tiers and add a gateway change to permit holding short-lived requests for 500ms for eligible keys.

Customer communicated workaround: gradual ramp-up or client-side limited concurrency (we provided a sample backoff snippet). Support recommends Atlas schedule job start with 10s stagger if they cannot change concurrency immediately.

SRE: Add alert for per-key burst_reservoir == 0 for dedicated/enterprise customers (owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-03-18).
DOCS: Update rate limit docs to clarify burst semantics for dedicated pools and example client patterns (owner: DevEx, ETA: 2026-03-24).
SUPPORT: Follow up with Atlas one week after production runs to confirm stability and close ticket (owner: Aisha, ETA: 2026-03-21).
